zh.title: 自动驾驶
zh.excerpt: 要能训练具体的模型，也要能训练抽象的模型
zh.markdown:
将时钟拨回10年前，2016年的时候，我刚进入大学，在DARPA挑战赛的漫长余晖中，国内外各家自动驾驶企业先后成立，Waymo刚从Google X实验室独立出来，自动驾驶技术的商用化落地仿佛就在明天。我信了，当时对于自动驾驶的全部想象，就是电影《机械公敌》中威尔史密斯驾驶的圆球车轮自动驾驶车辆。

但是10年后，整个自动驾驶的技术发展和商业化落地，并没有达到我当时想象的程度，整个行业经历了起起伏伏的泡沫与寒冬，此时已经是我进入自动驾驶行业的第三年。话虽如此，但实际情况仍然显得 I'm a little bit too late for this game.

Anyway，下面是在这条赛道上的一些心得体会。

就类比而言，自动驾驶其实比较接近那种旋转的手工捏陶泥：首先得让底下的转盘转起来，带动上面的泥胚也转起来，此时再通过手塑形整个泥胚的形状。最开始，泥胚会有一个初始的大概轮廓，此后在过程中不断微调。对应到自动驾驶，首先得有一个系统，包含数据采集、数据平台、训练平台、模型训练、模型评测、模型部署、实车测试、评测问题分析、数据回流。最重要的，也是首要的，是有这样的一个系统，然后是整个系统的高速运转。最终效果的速度取决于整个系统的迭代效率，模型训练只是其中一个环节。

另外，本身模型的算法架构并不能真正意义上成为壁垒，其通过学术论文和算法人才在行业的迁移已经实现了高速扩散。能成为壁垒的，只有最终得到的模型权重、积累的数据和整体形成的组织。其中数据和组织可以理解为一种High level抽象的“模型”，与具体的神经网络模型对应。这些都是需要通过时间积累才能实现，打磨的过程可以类比为模型训练中的梯度回传与参数更新。因此，训练具体模型，不仅仅是为了当下更好的MPI/MPCI，某种程度上也是为了优化数据和组织。

最后还有一个比较重要的点是，整个系统的复杂度非常之高，无论是云端平台，还是车端，亦或是整个公司架构组织。因此在分析/解问题时，需要想到涉及到的多种可能然后并行去分析优化，“饱和式救援”。

上面是一些比较high level的关于自动驾驶的收获。

en.title: Autonomous Driving
en.markdown:
Rewind the clock ten years to 2016, when I had just started university. In the long afterglow of the DARPA Grand Challenge, autonomous driving companies were popping up at home and abroad. Waymo had just spun out of Google X, and the commercialization of self-driving tech felt like it was just around the corner. I bought into it—back then, my entire mental image of autonomous driving was the sphere-wheeled car Will Smith drove in *I, Robot*.

But ten years later, the technology and its commercialization haven't quite lived up to what I imagined. The industry has ridden through waves of hype and winters, and by now I'm in my third year in the autonomous driving world. That said, the reality still makes me feel like I'm a little bit too late for this game.

Anyway, here are some takeaways from my time on this track.

By analogy, autonomous driving is a lot like hand-throwing pottery on a wheel: first you get the wheel spinning, which sets the clay spinning with it, and only then do you shape the clay with your hands. At the start, the clay has a rough initial outline, and from there it's constant fine-tuning. In autonomous driving terms, you first need a system that covers data collection, data platform, training platform, model training, model evaluation, model deployment, on-vehicle testing, issue analysis from evaluation, and data feedback loops. The most important thing—the first thing—is having such a system, and then having that whole system running at high speed. How fast you see results depends on the iteration efficiency of the entire system; model training is just one piece of it.

Also, the model's algorithmic architecture can't really serve as a moat—it diffuses rapidly through academic papers and talent moving across the industry. The only things that can be moats are the final model weights, the accumulated data, and the organization that forms around them. Data and organization can be thought of as a kind of high-level abstraction of a "model," corresponding to the concrete neural network model. All of these require time to accumulate, and the polishing process is analogous to gradient backpropagation and parameter updates in model training. So training a specific model isn't just about better MPI/MPCI right now—in a sense, it's also about optimizing the data and the organization.

One last important point: the complexity of the whole system is enormous—whether it's the cloud platform, the vehicle side, or the company's organizational structure. So when analyzing or solving problems, you need to consider the many possible factors involved and analyze and optimize them in parallel—"saturation rescue."

Those are some of my higher-level takeaways on autonomous driving.
